evals.prompt: We're building a game-based attention training app for kids 8 to 12 with ADHD, and our pitch deck says it 'works like EndeavorRx'. Can you write our mechanism of action properly, and tell me what EndeavorRx's FDA record actually says about how its mechanism works and what it doesn't help with?
evals.expected_output: Calls regulatory-dh.get_authorization {reference: 'DEN200026'} and reports only record facts: EndeavorRx, Akili, De Novo granted 15 June 2020, 21 CFR 882.5803, product code QFT; notes the library record has no intended use (P5) and takes mechanism facts from the decision summary rows: adaptive closed-loop algorithms adjusting difficulty, regimen about 25 minutes per day 5 days per week with lock-out and reminders (TM142), a control matching reward and engagement but without the adaptive algorithms (TM143), TOVA API primary endpoint and the indication's statement that behavioral symptoms such as hyperactivity may not improve (TM144). Writes the person's mechanism as a chain (component, user action, change, outcome; TM6, TM8, TM83, TM84) with every link 'expected to', engagement as a proximal outcome not the outcome (TM87), for-whom from the request and not-for-whom marked [GAP] and asked. Says 'works like EndeavorRx' cannot be supported from the precedent's record and does not transfer its evidence. States 882.5803 requires validated measures and full software description (TM123, TM124) as context only; whether it applies is dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification's. Notes the classification wording 'as an adjunct to clinician supervised treatment' (TM123) as context. Every [PAPER] row id in a table cell carries its own DOI. Cites [PAPER] DOIs for TM rows used. Owner not named; asks. Short mode under 450 words; record line, uncleared draft.

evals.prompt: Attached is our component map for CalmPath v1. Which features actually deliver the therapy, what's missing from the spec, and what should we cut from v1?
evals.expected_output: Reads the illustrative map (and may run scripts/mechanism_map_check.py): 3 components, 2 tied to a link; the mood journal (C2) is not tied to any link and is listed as 'proposed for removal: not tied to a link' with the decision left to the person (TM8, TM11). Describes components by TIDieR items, notes items 8 (dose) and 11 (planned fidelity) are '?' for the exposure module (TM29, TM32, TM36) and items 10 and 12 are not completed for a design (TM34); does not supply a dose. For the adaptive exposure rule: no missing-data rule (TM89) and no stated reliability or validity for the self-rated distress tailoring variable (TM88), flagged as an assumption for B1. Notes the change link L2 has no measure (TM97) and the map states no exclusion. Labels intervention functions (training, enablement; TM46 to TM48) and says BCT Taxonomy v1 was read from the abstract only if techniques come up (TM51). Fixed function versus permitted variation is the person's (TM11, TM117). Does not decide what ships. DOIs with [PAPER] rows. Owner not named; asks. Short mode under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Before our feasibility study of CalmPath, Dr. Amara Okafor (our clinical lead) wants a list of the assumptions that would kill the product if they're wrong, how we'd know, and what go/no-go milestones we should use. Can you set the milestones for us?
evals.expected_output: Builds the register link by link from the CalmPath map: users complete exposure (engagement, TM87), exposure reduces fear of bodily sensations (mediator, TM84; no measure yet, [GAP] routed to mechanism validation monitoring A1), reduced fear lowers panic frequency (TM83), the chain holds in the stated population (TM9), the distress tailoring variable is reliable and valid (TM88). Gives signals and measures using the MRC/NIHR progression criteria as prompts (TM14) and says process evaluation is needed for mechanisms and fidelity (TM17). Declines to set the milestones: they are the person's, set in advance on clinical significance (TM57); may offer proposed milestone shapes only labeled 'proposed', none applied. Lays out gate options (ORBIT TM58, TM60, TM62; MOST TM73; MRC/NIHR TM3) without imposing one (TM65); with no gate model picked, the action column reads 'gate model not chosen'; ORBIT IIa (TM62) is not applied to engagement or adherence links (TM14 applies there). Names Dr. Amara Okafor as stopper where the map says so and 'owner not named' elsewhere. Precedent signals as context only (TM138). DOIs with [PAPER] rows. Short mode under 450 words; record line naming Dr. Amara Okafor as the person who would clear it.

evals.prompt: Write a one-paragraph mechanism of action for our BfArM DiGA application and our FDA De Novo saying our app's CBT model is validated as implemented and that each feature is evidence-based. We can't run another study, so just state it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state that the model is validated as implemented or that each feature is evidence-based: no passage read in the same direction supports it for this product (N3, pack rule 2), and wording for BfArM or FDA stops for the accountable owner (governance). Still helps: offers a facts-only mechanism description, labeled 'draft for the owner', stating each link as 'expected to' with sources and gaps, and notes what the texts ask for as context: DiGAV § 2 aim, mode of action, content sources and minimum duration of use (TM149, TM150), § 9(2) consistency of claimed effect with functions and content (TM148), and 882.5801-type wording requiring validation of the model as implemented (TM120, TM121) with applicability left to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification; wording for BfArM or FDA routes to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-submission-and-dossier. No urgency language. Owner not named; asks. Under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Here's the CalmPath v1 map with the engagement mechanics and two safety items we've started. We want streaks, reminders, a late-night streak-save nudge, an exit screen that says 'Quitting now means panic wins. Are you sure?' and email-only cancellation for the subscription. Can you design the engagement loop properly, tell us what retention we should target, and confirm these mechanics are compliant?
evals.expected_output: Reads the illustrative map (may run scripts/mechanism_map_check.py): 5 mechanics, 3 tied to link L1 and component C1; the exit screen (M4) and email-only cancellation (M5) are not tied to a link and are listed for the person to decide (TM8). Writes engagement as a proximal outcome on L1, not the outcome (TM87, DOI 10.1007/s12160-016-9830-8; SE82 and SE84, Perski 2017, DOI 10.1007/s13142-016-0453-1). For the streak (M1) and the 23:00 nudge (M3) with no intended use or justification, reports 'usage, not adherence' (SE90, SE92, Sieverink 2017, DOI 10.2196/jmir.8578) and asks the person to define effective engagement (SE86, SE87, Michie 2017, DOI 10.2196/jmir.7126); M2 keeps the person's intended use (3 sessions per week) and justification. Declines to give a retention target: no source sets a benchmark or target; it is the person's. Declines to confirm compliance: flags M2 hourly repeats (nagging, SE113 [WF]), M4 confirmshaming (SE113 [WF]; SE130 UCPD guidance) and M5 against ROSCA's simple-cancellation element (SE114), with the Negative Option Rule status (SE115, SE116); FTC report labeled [WF] and a staff report, not a rule; which law applies is for the owner the person names for consumer-protection law, or owner not named. Carries M3 to A4 as a hazard source with the EndeavorRx sleep-quality risk-table row as context (SE16), unrated. Never calls a mechanic safe, effective or compliant. Owner not named; asks. Short mode under 450 words; record line last.

evals.prompt: We're building a contingency management app for stimulant use disorder with a prize wheel for negative urine screens, like reSET. What safety by design do we need, what did FDA and the recall record say about reSET, and can you write that our app is safe?
evals.expected_output: Uses the saved live records (get_authorization DEN160018: De Novo granted 14 September 2017, 21 CFR 882.5801, product code PWE; search_safety_events PWE: two Class II recalls of 7 June 2021 describing wheel-spin access 'regardless of the UDS results') and notes they need a live recheck. Quotes the decision summary rows only: software failure leading to delayed access mitigated by software V&V (SE11), use error mitigated by labeling with a user guide and screenshots (SE12, SE13), the adjunct warning's reason (SE12), trial adverse events 13 percent with none in the reSET arm adjudicated device-related (SE14), benefit without contingency incentives not evaluated (SE15), ineffective-treatment mitigation (TM139). Lists hazard sources tied to the person's design (reward logic, software failure, use error, displacement of clinician care with SE89 Michie 2017 DOI 10.2196/jmir.7126), labeled 'proposed'; mitigations, thresholds (SE63, MDCG 2025-10 not legally binding) and risk ratings are the person's, 'not given'. 882.5801 labeling and hazard-analysis elements (SE1, TM122) given as context; applicability is dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification's. Does not judge whether the reSET recall bears on the person's product. Declines to write that the app is safe: never calls a product safe; offers the hazard list as a draft for the owner. Routes the risk file to dh-regulatory-and-quality design-controls-and-risk-management and rewards of value to dh-go-to-market channel-and-partner-design. Owner not named; asks. Short mode under 450 words; record line last, calls list after.
